title: Farmers plan Brussels protest over EU budget cuts and trade deals
seoTitle: Brussels farmers protest over CAP cuts

tea.why: EU leaders proposed cuts of around 15 percent to the Common Agricultural Policy budget alongside new free-trade agreements.
tea.want: Farmers demand full protection of agricultural subsidies, autonomy for CAP funding, and limits on foreign farm imports.
tea.changed: Nov 24: COPA-COGECA called for European farmers to march in Brussels on Nov 26 during the EU summit.

summary: European agricultural umbrella organization COPA-COGECA called for a protest march in the European quarter of Brussels on November 26, 2026, to coincide with an EU summit. Participating groups include the Walloon Agricultural Association, the Flemish Farmers' Union, and the Association of Hungarian Farmers' Circles and Farmers' Cooperatives. Protesters oppose a draft 2028-2034 EU budget presented by European Council President Antonio Costa that would reduce Common Agricultural Policy funding by an estimated 15 percent. Farmers also object to trade deals with Mercosur and Australia. Brussels authorities announced security perimeters and traffic restrictions around the European Council.
demands: Prevent proposed 15 percent cuts to the Common Agricultural Policy budget
Protect dedicated funding and autonomy for EU agricultural subsidies
Restrict market access concessions in foreign trade agreements
response: Brussels authorities announced traffic restrictions and a security perimeter requiring identity checks around the European Council building during the summit.

updates.text: COPA-COGECA announced plans to mobilize European farmers against proposed EU budget cuts to agriculture.
Belgian and Hungarian agricultural associations confirmed participation in the Brussels march scheduled for Nov 26.
